limits: THE THIRD REGISTRATION FOR THIS GATE, and it exists because the anchor the subject needs DETECTS a sibling control's known-bad input. The verdict for #1155 asked for these cases to extend `controls/flow-finish-gate-declared-gates`. Measured instead of assumed, and they cannot: that control is anchored on af348f8 and covers `fail (declared but never ran: ...)`, while the honest anchor HERE is e7c8708 - the gate carrying #1147's guards and not #1155's reconciliation, which is the precise version blind to this defect and nothing wider. Run against the sibling's `bad-declared-never-ran` case, e7c8708 exits 1 and names it; an anchor that catches a control's known-bad input makes that case INERT, so one control cannot hold both subjects. Reported to the orchestrator rather than resolved either way in silence. WHAT THIS ESTABLISHES: that a manifest which leaves a declared gate OUT OF A PLAN makes the finish gate fail and name it. `.claude/cicd_tasks.yml` wins over BUILTIN_PLANS, so a dropped gate never runs AND is never recorded as skipped - it is absent from every channel the other checks read, which is why they all pass over it and the marker reads `ok`. WHAT IT DOES NOT ESTABLISH: that the gate set itself is right (the sibling control), that `make verify` is run at all (controls/flow-finish-gate), or anything about the Makefile fallback, which has no runner JSON and no manifest and therefore no reconciliation to do. THREE STATES, THREE CASES, because the third is the one a reader would otherwise never see: `bad-gate-dropped-from-plan` carries `"dropped_gates": ["verify"]`; `good-reconciled` carries `[]`; and `good-plan-not-reconcilable` carries `null` for a plan no built-in declares. `null` is NOT `[]` - there is no declaration to compare against, which is a different fact from having compared and found nothing missing. Rendering them alike would let a plan nobody can check report exactly what a clean plan reports, which is unscanned reading as clean. The not-applicable case is registered GOOD because there is no finding to make, and the reader still says so BY NAME on stderr; that the NAMING happens is pinned in tests/test_flow_finish_gate.py, since a control can only score the marker and the exit. THE CASES DESCEND FROM A FIELD ARTIFACT: they are built from the verbatim runner JSON captured for #1147's control, with the step and gate data unchanged and `dropped_gates` added, because a payload predating the field now exercises the reconciliation-unavailable branch rather than this one. ISOLATION (attachment coupling, 2026-09-22): cases run through the shared runner controls/flow-finish-gate/run-case.sh, which copies the case outside every git repository before running the gate. They previously ran IN PLACE inside this checkout, so the gate read the ENCLOSING repository's git state - a fact the fixture never chose - looked for a counter-model receipt on that branch, found none, and this control's GOOD case failed. Measured at one sha: attached to a branch -> fail, DETACHED at the same sha -> ok, attached to main -> fail. ATTACHMENT is the variable, so main fails permanently and CI, always detached, can never see it. Only GOOD cases were contaminated: a failing gate step short-circuits before the counter-model check, so every BAD case redded correctly in place. NO detect_signal CHANGED in that work - the anchor causes none of these failures and -derivation is anchored AND passed both ways, which refutes it as the cause.

anchors.why: The gate as it stood at e7c8708 - the merge of #1147 - vendored byte-for-byte. Chosen over the older af348f8 that the sibling controls use because it is the TIGHTEST anchor available: it already carries #1147's published gate set and its declared-but-never-ran guard, so the only thing it lacks is this issue's reconciliation. An anchor blind for many reasons demonstrates less than one blind for exactly this one. Measured on all three cases: it prints `FLOW_FINISH_GATE: ok` and exits 0 on the known-bad input, which it cannot do otherwise since nothing in it compares the resolved plan against the built-in declaration, and it agrees with the fixed gate on both known-good ones. Vendored rather than resolved from git at run time because git is absent from the negative-controls image; vendored again here rather than shared with the sibling control because the tracking check enumerates files under each control directory, and a path reaching out of one is untracked from that control's point of view (#978).
